 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 01, 2026, 12:53:04 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: India may look at a few changes to their playing XI when they face New Zealand in the fifth and final T20I on Sunday. Despite taking an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series, the team management will not be happy with the 87-run defeat in Auckland. 
 The Indian team management has backed its established players throughout the series. However, the heavy defeat in the fourth T20I could lead to some changes as the world champions look to finish the series with a win. 
 One of the big questions will be whether Vaibhav Sooryavanshi returns to the playing XI. If that happens, Sanju Samson could be the player making way. 
 Will Sooryavanshi replace Samson? 
 Samson has received backing from the team management, but his performances in the series have been inconsistent. 
 After scoring 67 in the opening match, the wicketkeeper-batter has managed scores of 14, 18 and four in his next three innings. 
 The team management could consider giving him a break and bringing back Sooryavanshi, who has already shown what he can do at the top of the order. 
 The youngster got opportunities in the second and third T20Is after Ishan Kishan was ruled out due to injury. However, he made way for Kishan when the latter returned to the team. 
 India vs New Zealand: Squads 
 India: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wk), Tilak Varma (vice-captain), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav. 
 New Zealand: Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Bevon Jacobs, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Devon Conway, Mitchell Santner (captain), Michael Bracewell, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner, Matt Fisher, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy, Adam Milne, Josh Clarkson. Commentary

 12:21 (IST) Nov 01 A quick chat with the Indian head coach - Scott Styris has caught up with Gautam Gambhir. Gautam acknowledges the short turnaround after the West Indies series but gives credit to the boys for adapting to the conditions, especially with many of them playing here for the first time. He says they are well aware of how dangerous New Zealand can be in their own backyard and insists there is no room for complacency, even with the series sealed. Believes every game offers an opportunity to learn something different and evolve, adding that there are no dead rubbers in his philosophy or within the team. On his approach to selection and decision-making, he says it is not his job to make everyone happy or take popular decisions. In today's day and age, with social media scrutiny, it is easy to make popular calls, but he believes in making the right decisions and giving players a longer rope to ensure they have security within the dressing room.

 12:03 (IST) Nov 01 The skipper of India - Shreyas Iyer calls it a great occasion to play at this historic ground. He says they were going to bat first anyway, as they wanted to test themselves and get a feel for how the wicket behaves in the first innings. Adds that the dimensions in Auckland were different, but gives credit to Glenn Phillips for playing an incredible knock. Confirms two changes, with Varun Chakaravarthy and Bhuvneshwar Kumar coming in. Says Chakaravarthy has been waiting for his opportunity and even delivered a beautiful speech in the team huddle today.
 12:03 (IST) Nov 01 The captain of New Zealand - Mitchell Santner is a bit surprised and cheekily says he just assumed he would lose the toss. Opts to bowl first and says that it looks like a new pitch and there might be a bit of dew later on. Santner adds that it is a challenge with the small grounds in New Zealand, but you have to adapt quickly to different dimensions. Reckons if there is some bounce like Eden Park, it would be nice. Mitch mentions that there was obviously something in the wicket in the last game which the seamers enjoyed. Informs that they have made one change, with Blair Tickner coming in for Matthew Fisher.
 12:03 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: TOSS New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner opts to field vs India in Hamilton 11:56 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: Glenn Phillips eyes another big score New Zealand will hope Glenn Phillips continues his fine form. He struck a brilliant century in Auckland and has been their most productive batter in the series.
 According to CricViz, Phillips has scored 276 runs in four matches. Only Mark Chapman, with 290 runs against Pakistan in 2023, has scored more for New Zealand in a five-match bilateral T20I series.
 The all-format record belongs to England wicketkeeper-batter Phil Salt, who scored 331 runs against the West Indies in 2023. Phillips needs another 56 runs to go past that mark.
 Michael Bracewell is another player in good touch after hitting a fifty in Auckland.
 11:44 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: Kuldeep, Varun could be in contention India could also look at bringing in a specialist wrist-spinner. Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule hinted that Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakravarthy could get an opportunity in Hamilton if the conditions demand it.
 However, including either of them would mean leaving out Dhir. That would reduce India's batting depth and also take away a part-time off-spin option.
 11:30 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: Will Vaibhav Sooryavanshi replace Sanju Samson? The most likely change could be the return of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, with Sanju Samson making way. Samson scored 67 in the series opener in Christchurch but has managed just 14, 18 and 4 in his next three innings.
 Captain Shreyas Iyer is also looking for runs. Since scoring his maiden T20I hundred against the West Indies in Lucknow, he has had a lean run, with scores of 40, 1, 16, 22, 42, 7, 5 and 22 in his last eight innings in the format.
 Iyer will be eager to finish the series with a big score before shifting his focus to the ODIs. Naman Dhir and Nitish Kumar Reddy have added value with their late-order hitting, but neither has made a significant contribution with the ball.
 11:13 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: India seek winning finish India could make a few changes to their playing XI when they face New Zealand in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park on Sunday. The visitors have already taken an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series, but their 87-run defeat in Auckland may prompt the team management to rethink its combination.
 India will be keen to end the series with a win before turning their attention to the ODI leg of the tour.
 11:05 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: Santner has the edge over Axar Patel The contest between the two left-arm spinners could also play an important role in the final match. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has enjoyed a productive series, while Axar Patel has had a contrasting approach with the ball.
 Axar has bowled at an average speed of 97 kph, compared to Santner's 89 kph. Santner has bowled fuller deliveries 55 per cent of the time and shorter ones 45 per cent. Axar, on the other hand, has bowled shorter 72 per cent of the time and fuller deliveries only 28 per cent.
 With Hamilton also being a small venue, how the two spinners handle the conditions could be a key factor in deciding which team ends the series on a winning note.

 10:40 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: New Zealand want to carry winning momentum Although India have already won the series, New Zealand will be keen to finish on a positive note.
 The hosts will want to take confidence from a victory in the final T20I before the upcoming five-match ODI series against India.
 The ODI series will be important for both teams as they look to assess their combinations and prepare for next year's ICC World Cup.
 New Zealand will also take confidence from the performances of Glenn Phillips and Michael Bracewell in Auckland. Phillips scored a century, while Bracewell produced a powerful half-century to help the hosts register a big win.
 India, meanwhile, will look to put that defeat behind them and end the T20I series on a winning note.

 10:19 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: Kuldeep Yadav or Varun Chakravarthy in contention? India's bowling department also has a few issues to address.
 The team has depended heavily on Arshdeep Singh for wickets, while Axar Patel has provided some control. The much-anticipated return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar has not produced the expected results so far.
 The experienced pacer has taken just one wicket in three matches and conceded 139 runs at an economy rate of 11.58. Arshdeep is the only Indian bowler with an economy rate below 10 in the series.
 India could consider bringing in either Kuldeep Yadav or Varun Chakravarthy to strengthen the spin attack.
 However, making room for another specialist bowler could mean dropping Naman Dhir. That would reduce India's batting depth and also take away an option for part-time off-spin.
 Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule has said that both Kuldeep and Chakravarthy are ready to play whenever the team needs them. However, it remains to be seen whether either of them gets an opportunity in the final T20I.
 India could also look at using Tilak Varma and Abhishek Sharma as additional bowling options, but that could be a risky move given the scoring pattern in the series.
 10:18 (IST) Nov 01 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 5th T20I: Shreyas Iyer needs a big score Captain Shreyas Iyer is another player who will be keen to make an impact in the final match.
 Iyer had started his T20I journey with a century, but his numbers in the next eight innings have not been impressive. He has scored 40, 1, 16, 22, 42, 7, 5 and 22 in those matches.
 His struggles have not received much attention because Naman Dhir and Nitish Kumar Reddy have played some important late-order knocks in recent matches.
 However, Iyer will be aware that he needs a substantial innings to regain his touch and confidence.
